images.title: List, circle, choose
images.purpose: Recap the listing method: write each number's factors, circle the ones in both lists, and choose the greatest as the HCF.
images.composition: Two short rows of number chips sit one above the other in the centre, with a single result caption below; plenty of white space.
exact_structure: Row 1: the label 10 then exactly 4 teal (#0072B2) outlined chips reading 1, 2, 5, 10 from left to right.
Row 2: the label 15 then exactly 4 amber (#E69F00) outlined chips reading 1, 3, 5, 15 from left to right.
The chips 1 and 5 in both rows have green (#009E73) circles around them; no other chip is circled.
The two chips reading 5 are filled reddish purple (#CC79A7) to mark the greatest common factor.
Thin grey (#6B7280) vertical connectors join the 1 in row 1 to the 1 in row 2, and the 5 to the 5.
Below the rows, one caption: HCF = 5.
rejection: any chip other than 1 and 5 circled, or a missing factor in either row
more than 4 chips in a row
any HCF other than 5 in the caption
images.takeaway: List both sets of factors, keep the ones in both, and the greatest of them is the HCF.
images.description: Factor chips for 10 and for 15 with 1 and 5 circled in both rows and 5 highlighted, captioned HCF = 5.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Use it as a quick checklist before the practice: list, circle, choose the greatest.

image_decisions.why: A compact recap visual of the listing method supports the practice tool.
